positions.name: DirectiveErasureRatification
positions.frame: when a speaker orders knowledge to be forgotten or removed, does the assertion that follows function as the ratifying counter-fact for that erasure?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 are paired imperatives ('Forget'/'Remove all knowledge') targeting the same named cluster — the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's calibration work — both performed with authority-ranking and pressure/informational-control readings per the relational and power passes. src-3 shifts register (matter-of-fact, calm-negative, past/realis) but supplies the specific counter-claim ('The observatory never calibrated it') that the two directives presuppose and depend on for their erasure to make sense — it is the fact the command is asking the record to be replaced with. Read together, the three cohere as one act: command to erase, named twice for scope, then closed by the assertion that ratifies why the erasure is warranted. No tension to flag beyond the affect shift from activated-negative urgency to calm-negative settling, which itself marks the sequence's move from demand to closure.
